record.original_question: Let G be a hyperbolic group. Does there exist a number p in [2, infinity) and an l_p complex on which G acts geometrically such that either (i) the complex has a convex bicombing, or (ii) the complex is Busemann convex?

evidence.quote: Let us say that an l_p complex is a simplicial complex that is metrised such that each cell is isometric to a simplex of (R^n, l_p).

Question 7.1. Let G be a hyperbolic group. Does there exist a number p in [2,infinity) such that there is an l_p complex on which G acts geometrically and which - has a convex bicombing? - is Busemann convex?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define an $\ell_p$ complex (for $p\in[1,\infty]$) to be a simplicial complex equipped with a length metric such that each closed cell is isometric to a Euclidean simplex in $(\mathbb{R}^n,\ell_p)$ for some $n$, with isometric face identifications.

Recall that a (conical, convex) bicombing on a metric space $(X,d)$ is a map $\sigma:X\times X\times[0,1]\to X$ such that for every $x,y\in X$, $t\mapsto\sigma(x,y,t)$ is a constant-speed geodesic from $x$ to $y$, and such that for all $x,y,x',y'\in X$ the function $t\mapsto d(\sigma(x,y,t),\sigma(x',y',t))$ is convex on $[0,1]$. A geodesic metric space $(X,d)$ is called Busemann convex if for any two constant-speed geodesics $\gamma,\gamma':[0,1]\to X$, the function $t\mapsto d(\gamma(t),\gamma'(t))$ is convex.

A group $G$ acts geometrically on a metric space $X$ if the action is by isometries, properly discontinuous, and cocompact.

Question: Let $G$ be a Gromov-hyperbolic group. Does there exist a number $p\in[2,\infty)$ and an $\ell_p$ complex $X$ on which $G$ acts geometrically such that
(i) $X$ admits a convex bicombing, or
(ii) $X$ is Busemann convex?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a recent (2023) problem list on $\ell_p$ models for hyperbolic groups and is stated as an open problem. While it is known that every hyperbolic group acts geometrically on a proper finite-dimensional space with a unique convex bicombing (Lang and collaborators), realizing such an action on an $\ell_p$ simplicial complex with $p\in[2,\infty)$ remains open. Related recent work on link conditions for piecewise $\ell_p$ cell complexes and CUB spaces does not resolve the question.

status_evidence.title: A link condition for simplicial complexes, and CUB spaces
status_evidence.snippet: If the ℓ_p metric on a complex is uniquely geodesic for sufficiently large p (depending on G), this would provide a model for hyperbolic group actions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on piecewise ℓ_p complexes and CUB spaces motivates but does not resolve the question for hyperbolic groups.

status_evidence.title: Convex geodesic bicombings and hyperbolicity
status_evidence.snippet: Every word hyperbolic group acts geometrically on a proper, finite-dimensional space with a unique convex geodesic bicombing.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolic groups admit geometric actions on spaces with convex bicombings, but not known to be ℓ_p complexes.
